subject: CPLT
course_description: This course draws on classical, modern, and contemporary texts to introduce skills required for reading comparatively across national traditions and academic disciplines with an emphasis on close reading, critical interpretation, and the multiplicity of linguistic traditions around the world. *Note: This course is non-repeatable.
course_notes: Course topic: Hauntologies: Tragic Experience and Traumatic Memory This course will explore some of the ways that trauma, both individual and collective, is represented, appropriated, and allegorized in the tropes of literary and genre fiction with particular attention to works which blur the lines between the supernatural and the psychological. The texts and media covered in the course will include classical and early modern tragic drama, 19th and 20th century gothic literature, and 20th and 21st century film, television, and comics, including works by Euripides, Shakespeare, Poe, James, Morrison, Moore & Gibbons's Watchmen and the 2019 Watchmen televisual adaptation. This course will work through these texts and themes with a variety of theoretical approaches, drawing on texts from Aristotle, Freud, Marx, Kristeva, and Derrida.
